title: セールストークのコツ  (The Trick to Sales Talk)

segments.t: Sitting down after those failed doorbell calls, Ono suddenly praises Muranishi for supporting his wife, two children, and mother all by himself. The moment Muranishi brightens up, Ono grins—he was demonstrating the secret of sales talk. Listen to Ono's lesson.
まあ、でもお前は頑張ってるよ。
嫁さんと子供二人とおふくろさんを食べさせてるんだろ？
立派だよ、本当に。根性もあるしな。
ありがとうございます。
一瞬やる気になったろ？
これがセールストークの基本だ。
褒めて相手を口説くんだよ。
褒めて、褒めて、心を開かせろ。
なるべく丁寧な言葉でな。
英語の教材を売ってるんだから英語を使え。
お恥ずかしながら、私、イングリッシュは苦手で。
難しく考えるな。何でもいいから単語を言えばいいんだよ。
Ono gives Muranishi a masterclass in human psychology—and gives us a treasure chest of everyday expressions.
まあ、でもお前は頑張ってるよ。
'Well, still, you are working really hard.' "Ganbatteru" comes from "ganbaru", to hang in there and give your best effort—one of the warmest things a colleague can tell you.
嫁さんと子供二人とおふくろさんを食べさせてるんだろ？

'You are feeding your wife, two kids, and your mum, right?' Casual "yomesan" means a man's wife, "futari" counts two people, and affectionate "ofukurosan" means one's mother. "Tabesaseteru" turns "taberu", to eat, into 'feeding and supporting'.
立派だよ、本当に。
'That is admirable, truly.' "Rippa" praises someone as splendid, worthy of respect, or standing tall, reinforced by "hontou ni", truly.
一瞬やる気になったろ？
'For a second there, you felt motivated, right?' "Yaruki" glues "yaru", to do, onto "ki", spirit—literally 'doing-spirit', the everyday word for motivation!
これがセールストークの基本だ。
'This is the foundation of sales talk.' "Kihon" means the basics or foundation of any craft, sport, or skill.
褒めて相手を口説くんだよ。
'You praise the other person and win them over.' "Aite" means the person across from you—your listener, partner, or customer—and "homete" links "homeru", to praise, into "kudoku", to woo or persuade.
褒めて、褒めて、心を開かせろ。
'Praise them, praise them, and make them open their heart.' "Kokoro" is heart or mind, and "hirakasero" turns "hiraku", to open, into a command meaning 'make them open up!'
なるべく丁寧な言葉でな。
'Using as polite language as possible, mind you.' "Narubeku" means 'as much as possible', paired with "teinei na kotoba", polite words.
お恥ずかしながら、私、イングリッシュは苦手で。
'Embarrassing as it is, English is my weak point.' Funny irony: Muranishi calls English "ingurisshu" while admitting it is "nigate", something you are bad at or uncomfortable with.
難しく考えるな。
'Do not overthink it.' Changing "muzukashii", difficult, to "muzukashiku" before "kangaeru na", do not think, literally says 'do not think difficultly'—'do not overcomplicate it!'
何でもいいから単語を言えばいいんだよ。

'Just say any single words at all.' "Nandemo ii" means 'anything is fine', and "tango" means individual vocabulary words rather than full sentences. Now let's hear Ono's whole sales-talk secret again.
まあ、でもお前は頑張ってるよ。
嫁さんと子供二人とおふくろさんを食べさせてるんだろ？
立派だよ、本当に。根性もあるしな。
ありがとうございます。
一瞬やる気になったろ？
これがセールストークの基本だ。
褒めて相手を口説くんだよ。
褒めて、褒めて、心を開かせろ。
なるべく丁寧な言葉でな。
英語の教材を売ってるんだから英語を使え。
お恥ずかしながら、私、イングリッシュは苦手で。
難しく考えるな。何でもいいから単語を言えばいいんだよ。

Hold on to "yaruki" for motivation, "nigate" when you want to say you are not good at something, and "nandemo ii" whenever anything will do. Let's see Muranishi test this advice at a giant mansion next.
また明日。
